claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

Let's start: **How many children are you claiming Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm wanting to claim for my son Alex. He's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're welcome! Happy to help you with your Child Benefit claim for Alex.

Let me ask you a few more questions to assess your eligibility:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the situation a bit more.

**Could you tell me why Alex doesn't live with you? For example, is he living with another family member, in hospital, in local authority care, or in another arrangement?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

**Are you contributing towards the cost of Alex's upkeep? For example, do you pay maintenance or contribute at least the same amount as the current Child Benefit rate (which is £26.05 per week for the eldest or only child)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with things like his clothes, school supplies, and activities - I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you, that's helpful to know.

**Is Alex's mum (your ex-partner) currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not certain if she's claiming it or not. Is that something that would affect whether I can claim?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, it does matter. Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any one time. If two people claim for the same child, Child Benefit is usually paid to the person the child lives with.

Since Alex lives with his mum, she would generally have priority for receiving Child Benefit, even if you are contributing towards his upkeep.

**To help me give you a complete picture, can I also confirm: are you living in the UK, and do you have the right to live in the UK (for example, through citizenship, settled status, or a valid visa)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester. I'm a British citizen, so no issues with my right to live here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have a clear picture of your situation.

Based on the rules for Child Benefit, I need to explain something important:

**Only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child at any one time.** When a child lives with someone else (like your ex-partner), there are specific rules:

1. If no one else is claiming, you could potentially get Child Benefit for 8 weeks after a child goes to live with someone else, and it can continue longer if you contribute to the child's upkeep (at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit rate).

2. **However**, if two people try to claim for the same child, Child Benefit is paid to the person the child lives with — in this case, that would be Alex's mum.

Since Alex lives with his mum full-time, she has priority for receiving Child Benefit. Even though you're contributing £30 per week towards Alex's upkeep (which is above the Child Benefit rate), this would only allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit if you were *already* receiving it before Alex went to live elsewhere.

If Alex's mum claims (or is already claiming) Child Benefit, her claim would take priority because Alex lives with her.

Let me now provide you with my formal assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## My Assessment

Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you are not eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Reason:

- **Alex lives with his mother**, your ex-partner
- Under Child Benefit rules, **only one person can receive Child Benefit for a child**
- When two people could potentially claim, **priority goes to the person the child lives with**
- While your weekly contributions of £30 are commendable and exceed the Child Benefit rate, this doesn't give you priority over Alex's mother — contributions towards upkeep only help maintain an *existing* Child Benefit claim when a child moves to live elsewhere

### What this means:

Alex's mother is the person entitled to claim Child Benefit for him because he lives with her. If she's not currently claiming, she should consider doing so.

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. If you have any questions or if your circumstances change in the future (for example, if Alex comes to live with you), please don't hesitate to revisit your eligibility. Is there anything else I can help you with?
